items.note: a higher view than the Needle, with the Needle in the shot. A better skyline photo on gray days.

items.name: Kubota Garden
items.note: free Japanese garden, open sunrise to sundown every day, including Monday. 100th anniversary in 2027.

items.name: Seattle Japanese Garden
items.note: closed December-February for winter maintenance, so save it for a spring trip.

items.name: Washington Park Arboretum
items.note: free, open daily. Winter-flowering witch hazel and camellias, and easy paved paths in the rain.

items.name: Volunteer Park Conservatory
items.note: Victorian glasshouse that's warm and dry inside, $6. Tue-Sun 10-4 (closed Mon). Right next to SAAM.

items.name: Snoqualmie Falls
items.note: 268-ft falls at its fullest in the December rain. Upper viewpoint plus a short trail down. Low elevation, no snow gear.

items.name: Bainbridge Island ferry
items.note: 35-minute ride with skyline views from the deck; you only pay westbound, and a walk-on is cheap. Time it for a 3:30-4 PM sunset crossing back.

items.name: Discovery Park
items.note: bluffs over Puget Sound and the West Point lighthouse. Large, so stay on the main loop in daylight.

items.name: Alki Beach
items.note: skyline-across-the-water shot plus a beach walk. Fits your coast-over-mountains preference.

items.name: Hing Hay Park
items.note: Chinese pavilion and dragon mural, the photo heart of the ID.

items.name: Seattle Great Wheel
items.note: enclosed gondolas, so it works in the rain. Pair it with the new waterfront promenade.

items.name: Beneath the Streets underground tour
items.note: indoor history tour of the buried old city. A rainy-day filler.

items.name: Green River Trail
items.note: flat paved river trail for a quick walk on any free morning.

items.name: Cedar River Trail
items.note: flat river path. Pair it with Renton Asian food.

items.name: Saltwater State Park
items.note: Needs a Discover Pass.

items.name: Seward Park
items.note: old-growth forest loop on a Lake Washington peninsula, flat and busy (safe).

items.name: Discovery Park Loop
items.note: 2.8-mile loop with Sound views from the bluff.

items.name: Lincoln Park
items.note: bluff forest and a beach walk with Olympics views.

items.name: Schmitz Preserve Park
items.note: short old-growth ravine near Alki. Pair it with Alki photos.

items.name: Coal Creek Falls
items.note: about 2.5 miles to a small waterfall that is fullest in winter, with low elevation.

items.name: Wildside Trail / De Leo Wall
items.note: mining-history forest loop. Muddy in winter.

items.name: Twin Falls
items.note: about 2.6 miles round trip to a big falls with a footbridge. Low elevation; combine with Snoqualmie Falls.

items.name: Little Si
items.note: about 3.7 miles round trip with a payoff view, steeper but short. Popular, so you won't be alone.

items.name: Rattlesnake Ledge
items.note: about 4 miles round trip, 1,160 ft gain, with a lake-and-valley view from the ledge. Very popular. Skip if there's ice, and stay back from the edge.

items.name: Point Defiance Park
items.note: forest loops and waterfront viewpoints. Pair it with the Tacoma museum day.

items.name: Ruston Way
items.note: flat 2-mile waterfront promenade, an easy coast walk.

items.name: Chinatown-International District
items.note: Uwajimaya, Kinokuniya, Daiso, Asian bakeries, Hing Hay Park.

items.name: Capitol Hill / Pike-Pine
items.note: vintage and streetwear shops, record stores, Elliott Bay Book Co., boba and cafes. Busy and walkable in daylight.

items.name: Fremont / Wallingford
items.note: Fremont Troll, quirky shops, a Sunday market, and Gas Works Park nearby. Good for photos.

items.name: Ballard
items.note: indie boutiques on Ballard Ave and the Ballard Locks (watch the boats lock through).

items.name: U District
items.note: student-priced Asian food, boba and K-food along the Ave. Pair it with the Henry and Burke museums.

items.name: University Village
items.note: open-air upscale mall with fashion and beauty shops, an easy rainy-afternoon browse.

items.name: Pioneer Square
items.note: brick-and-ivy historic core, galleries, Klondike museum, comic and game stores.

items.name: Queen Anne
items.note: Kerry Park plus quieter cafes and boutiques up the hill.

items.name: West Seattle / Alki
items.note: beach-town strip with skyline views, a half-day with a walk.

items.name: The Bellevue Collection
items.note: Bellevue Square, Lincoln Square and Bellevue Place. Luxury fashion, jewelry, skincare, and a strong Asian dining scene.

items.name: Downtown Bellevue
items.note: Downtown Park and the Asian food and boba corridors around it.

items.name: Tacoma
items.area: Museum District, Ruston Way, Point Defiance
items.note: a day trip pairing glass, car and art museums with the waterfront.

groups.title: South King County (Kent / Tukwila / Renton / Federal Way)

items.name: Iron Pot Korean
items.note: small, well-reviewed Korean lunch spot (bulgogi bibimbap, stone pots), cheap and fast before a day out.

items.name: Triumph Valley
items.note: sit-down Chinese with lunchtime dim sum in a big former steakhouse. Skip the hot pot sauce bar.

items.name: Kizuki Ramen & Izakaya
items.area: Tukwila, Westfield Southcenter; also Renton, Bellevue, Capitol Hill

items.name: Fort St. George
items.note: Japanese yoshoku diner for omurice, katsudon, cod roe udon and Japanese-style spaghetti. A real local favorite and cheap.

items.name: Maneki
items.note: one of Seattle's oldest restaurants (since 1904), with sushi and Japanese homestyle plates in tatami rooms. Book ahead; dinner only.

items.name: Onibaba
items.note: onigiri specialist from the old Tsukushinbo team. A quick, good solo lunch between Wing Luke and Kinokuniya.

items.name: Chengdu Taste
items.note: Sichuan (laziji chicken).

groups.title: Capitol Hill / Fremont / Belltown / Pike Place

items.name: Ramen Danbo
items.note: Fukuoka-style tonkotsu with custom firmness and richness. Expect a line, so go at an off hour.

items.name: Ooink
items.note: tiny ramen counter known for black garlic and mala kotteri. Mala has Sichuan peppercorn.

items.name: Menya Musashi
items.note: tsukemen and mazemen from the Tokyo chain.

items.name: Midnite Ramen
items.note: The Infatuation's #1 ramen in town (shoyu, wontonmen). It sits inside a brewery taproom, so go at lunch.

items.name: Kamonegi
items.note: handmade soba and tempura from a James Beard-nominated chef. The sit-down splurge pick.

items.name: Sushi Kashiba
items.note: omakase from Shiro Kashiba (a Jiro alum). Splurge, so book on Resy weeks ahead.

items.name: Shaoshan Impression
items.note: serious Hunan heat in a strip mall, rarely found outside big Chinese hubs.

items.name: Dan Gui
items.note: solid Sichuan, set up for a solo lunch. Sichuan means.

items.name: Sun Sui Wah
items.note: Vancouver's famous Cantonese seafood and dim sum house, opened in Bellevue in 2024.

items.name: Henry's Taiwan Kitchen
items.note: Taiwanese homestyle food (beef noodle soup, three-cup chicken).

items.name: Hokkaido Ramen Santouka
items.note: rich shio and miso ramen; pair it with Uwajimaya shopping.

items.name: CHICHA San Chen
items.area: Tukwila, near Southcenter; also Bellevue Square
items.note: Taiwanese brewed-to-order tea, voted Best Bubble Tea in the 2026 Best of Seattle Southside awards.

items.name: TP TEA
items.note: Taiwan brand (from the Chun Shui Tang lineage) with a long menu and toppings.

items.name: Natalie's Sugar Cane & Dessert
items.area: Tukwila, inside Lam's Seafood Asian Market
items.note: family-run Vietnamese shop with fresh-pressed sugar cane and housemade toppings. A true deep cut.

items.name: Neighborhood Cafe
items.note: Filipino-inspired boba (flan, pandan, banana), so you can grab one on the way out Monday.

items.name: Atulea
items.note: matcha lattes, purple rice and cheese-foam drinks, and soft serve. A Seattle Met and Infatuation pick.

items.name: Xing Fu Tang
items.note: Taiwanese brown sugar boba stir-fried in-store, fun to film.

items.name: Yi Fang Taiwan Fruit Tea
items.note: Taiwanese fruit tea and brown sugar lattes. Check the site for the nearest store.

items.name: Sharetea
items.area: U District 45th St; Des Moines near Tukwila
items.note: Taiwanese classic.

items.name: Floating Leaves Tea
items.note: small Taiwanese oolong importer with tastings and tea classes. A tea-over-coffee deep cut; email ahead for a session.

items.name: U District boba strip
items.note: the densest boba area in Seattle (Timeless Tea, Ding Tea, Boba Up and more), good for a crawl.

items.name: Fuji Bakery
items.area: CID 526 S King St; Interbay; Bellevue
items.note: Japanese bakery with matcha danishes, curry pan and ube or crunchy-cream malasadas. The CID shop fits a Wing Luke day.

items.name: Hood Famous Cafe
items.note: Filipino bakery famous for ube cheesecake and pan de ube. Daytime cafe Tue-Sun (bar paused, which suits you). One review site marks it closed, so call (206) 261-2066 first.

items.name: Tous les Jours
items.area: CID 625 5th Ave S; Bellevue 100 108th Ave NE
items.note: Korean-French bakery for cream breads and cakes.

items.name: 85°C Bakery Cafe
items.area: Tukwila, Westfield Southcenter; also Federal Way, Bellevue
items.note: Taiwanese bakery with sea-salt coffee and marble taro.

items.name: Paris Baguette
items.area: Tukwila 17095 Southcenter Pkwy; Federal Way, opened 7/2026; Bellevue

items.name: Kiki Bakery
items.note: Taiwanese bakery with milk breads and pork floss buns.

items.name: Mei Wa Bakery
items.area: Kent, inside Great Wall Shopping Mall at 18230 E Valley Hwy

items.name: Phin
items.note: Vietnamese coffee brewed one cup at a time with housemade condensed milk, plus waffles. The Infatuation calls it "extremely special.".

items.name: Hello Em
items.note: Vietnamese robusta and salted egg cream coffee, a Seattle Met 2026 pick.

items.name: Cardoon
items.note: blue-tiled Chinese-German cafe with specialty coffee and food. Very photogenic.

items.name: Analog Coffee
items.note: dialed-in espresso and a neighborhood favorite, near Danbo and Atulea.

items.name: Espresso Vivace
items.note: David Schomer's shop, which shaped Seattle latte art. A coffee-history stop.

items.name: Milstead & Co.
items.note: the gold-standard multi-roaster. Pair it with Kamonegi or the Fremont Troll.

items.name: Ghost Note Coffee
items.note: drinks built like alcohol-free cocktails with housemade syrups.

items.name: Anchorhead Coffee
items.note: matte-black cafes known for the "cakeboi" pastry, handy on a Pike Place morning.

items.name: Boon Boona Coffee
items.area: roastery in Renton, cafes in several places

items.name: Day Made Kaffe Bar
items.note: minimalist Scandinavian pour-overs, near Showbox SoDo for a pre-show stop.

items.name: Tet in Seattle
items.note: Vietnamese Lunar New Year. 2027: Jan 30-31.

items.name: CID Lunar New Year Celebration
items.note: lion dances and food walk. Usually late Feb or early March (2026: Mar 7).

items.name: Bellevue Collection Lunar New Year
items.note: lion dance and stage performances. Usually the weekend after LNY (2026: Feb 21; displays mid-Feb to Mar 1).

items.name: Seattle Cherry Blossom & Japanese Cultural Festival
items.note: taiko, tea, anime-adjacent culture. 2027: Apr 9-11.

items.name: Festál series
items.note: free cultural festivals. Asian ones in 2027: AANHPI Heritage May 8, A Glimpse of China May 15, Pagdiriwang Philippine Jun 5-6, A Day in Punjab Aug 7, Tibet Fest Aug 14-15, Diwali Nov 6, Hmong New Year Nov 13. No December dates.

items.name: Japan Fair
items.note: successor to Aki Matsuri, with Japanese culture, food and artisans. Late June (2026 was June 26-28, 10th year).

items.name: Seattle Bon Odori
items.area: Seattle Betsuin Buddhist Temple, Central District
items.note: Japanese street dance festival, free, a Seafair event. Mid-July (2026: Jul 18-19).

items.name: Uwajimaya Natsu Matsuri
items.note: summer festival with food and a Bon Odori lesson. Same weekend as Bon Odori (2026: Jul 18-19).

items.name: Seafair Chinatown Parade
items.note: evening lion and dragon parade. Mid-to-late July.

items.name: CID Night Market
items.note: free street festival with ~100 vendors, lion dances and taiko. Last Saturday of September (2026: Sep 26, 1-9 PM). Watch impulse spending.

items.name: Mid-Autumn Festival at Seattle Chinese Garden
items.note: free Moon Festival, mid-to-late September (2026: Sep 26).

items.name: Garden d'Lights
items.note: the one December lights event, Nov 28, 2026-Jan 3, 2027, 4:30-9 PM, about $10, timed tickets online only. After dark and crowded, but it's a ticketed, busy, family event, not a lonely trail.

items.name: Amy Yee Tennis Center
items.note: city-run, 10 indoor courts; same-day indoor bookings by phone (206-684-4764) or walk-in, no membership card needed for same-day.

items.name: Robinswood Tennis Center
items.note: city-run, 4 indoor courts, no membership; book by phone (425-452-7690) from 8:30 AM, up to 6 days ahead; 24-hr cancellation rule.

items.name: Topgolf Renton
items.note: covered, heated bays with ball-tracking games. Bays are priced per hour, so going solo costs more per person. It's also a bar, but non-drinkers are fine.

items.name: Interbay Golf Center
items.note: 80-stall covered, heated range, half with Toptracer; plus mini golf. Rain-proof.

items.name: Bill Wright Golf Complex at Jefferson Park
items.note: city range with Toptracer, 15 min from the ID; skyline views from the course.

items.name: Federal Way Discount Guns & Indoor Range
items.note: indoor range with a big rental fleet (160+ guns), good for trying several models. Call to confirm hours and rental rules: (253) 927-5229.

items.name: Bellevue Indoor Range
items.note: public indoor range attached to Wade's Eastside Guns; has gun rentals and bay reservations. Open Sun-Fri 10-8, Sat 10-9.

items.name: Easy Street Records & Cafe
items.note: the city's best-known record store, with a diner-style cafe attached, so you can make a meal of it.

items.name: Silver Platters SoDo
items.note: big new/used shop with lots of electronic and soundtrack stock; close to the stadiums.

items.name: Daybreak Records
items.note: used-vinyl dig spot; pairs with a Fremont wander.

items.name: Everyday Music
items.note: large used CD/vinyl shop in the Pike/Pine shopping core.

items.name: Round1 Bowling & Arcade
items.note: Japanese rhythm and crane games, bowling, private karaoke rooms. The easiest rainy-night option without the light rail.

items.name: Immersive Gamebox
items.note: motion-tracking game rooms that opened Aug 2026, from ~$27. Better with 2+ people, but solo sessions are possible.

items.name: Seattle Pinball Museum
items.note: pay once and play all the machines (~$23 adult); no bar scene; next to the ID food crawl.

items.name: The Ice Box Arcade
items.note: retro arcade with ~47 machines.

items.name: Add-A-Ball
items.note: largest vintage coin-op collection in the city, but it's a bar. Go for the games.

items.name: Raygun Lounge
items.note: board game cafe/lounge for solo drop-in tables. Bar on site; confirm hours before going.

items.name: Round1 Southcenter karaoke rooms
items.note: the best solo, no-bar karaoke pick.

items.name: Rock Box
items.note: Japanese-style private karaoke boxes for 2-15 people. It's a full bar, so check room minimums before booking solo.

items.name: Cardceus
items.note: top-rated Pokemon shop with English and Japanese sealed product and singles; weekly Pokemon night. Open Thu-Fri 12-8, Sat-Sun 1-9, closed Mon-Tue.

items.name: Mox Boarding House
items.note: huge TCG and board game store with a tournament hall; it's the Card Kingdom retail flagship, with a restaurant/bar inside.

items.name: Blue Highway Games
items.note: neighborhood game store carrying TCGs; easy to pair with Kerry Park.

items.name: Kinokuniya Seattle
items.note: biggest Japanese bookstore and manga selection in the Northwest, plus stationery and figures.

items.name: Uwajimaya
items.note: Japanese/Asian supermarket with snacks, gifts and beauty aisles.

items.name: TESO Life
items.note: Japanese-style lifestyle department store with skincare, snacks, collectible toys and mini building kits.

items.name: The Gundam Base Seattle
items.note: only the third official Gundam store in North America. Still "coming soon" as of late Nov 2026; check whether it has opened by 12/4.

items.name: SUKOSHI
items.note: curated Asian beauty store with 200+ makeup and skincare brands; opened Jan 2026, its first Washington store.

items.name: KOBO at Higo
items.note: Japanese and Northwest crafts, ceramics and jewelry in the historic Higo Variety Store building; holds about 6 exhibits a year. Fits the art-collecting hobby.

items.name: KOBO Capitol Hill
items.note: the original shop/gallery, Japanese-aesthetic gifts and art.

items.name: Storica Studio
items.note: independent, woman- and minority-owned jewelry store.

items.name: Valerie Madison
items.note: Seattle-made fine jewelry, ethically sourced stones.

items.name: America's Car Museum
items.note: 4-floor car museum next to the Tacoma Dome; check its events page for special exhibits. Pairs with the Museum of Glass.

items.name: LeMay Collections at Marymount
items.note: huge family car collection in a former military academy, with guided tours year-round.

items.name: Seattle Glassblowing Studio & Gallery
items.note: book-ahead "blow your own" session (ornament, paperweight, bowl etc.); pieces cool for 24-48 hrs, so do it Fri/Sat to pick up before leaving Mon. Groupon deals are common.

items.name: Glassybaby hot shop
items.note: hands-on glassblowing sessions, including a winter ornament session in past years (~$180, 12+). Check the 2026 dates.

items.name: Seattle Artist League
items.note: one-night "One Shot Pot" beginner wheel class (~$95 incl. materials) and other drop-in art classes; check the calendar for December dates.

items.name: Classpop Asian cooking classes
items.note: one-off ramen, dumpling and sushi classes (~$60-135); several December 2026 dates listed.

items.name: Cozymeal Asian cooking classes
items.note: book-ahead one-time chef-led classes (dumplings, Japanese, etc.).

items.name: Hipcooks Seattle
items.note: small hands-on cooking classes by date; check the calendar for a menu that fits.

items.name: Garnish Music Production School
items.note: one-to-one private lessons, including electronic music/DJ; good for a single in-person DJ session.

items.name: Seattle Kraken (NHL)
items.note: *home Sun 12/6 at 5 PM vs Buffalo Sabres*, which fits the free Sunday. Other home games are Dec 1, Dec 3 (Dallas) and Dec 10 (Washington).

items.name: Seattle Seahawks (NFL)
items.note: *home Mon 12/7 at 5:15 PM vs Dallas Cowboys* (Monday night). Expensive, but rare. It also means heavy SoDo and light rail traffic Monday evening. Other home games: Dec 13 Giants and Dec 25 Rams.

items.name: Seattle Thunderbirds (WHL junior hockey)
items.note: cheap, loud and close. Resale sites list *Sun 12/6 at 4:05 PM vs Victoria Royals*; confirm on the team site.

items.name: Seattle Torrent (PWHL women's hockey)
items.note: season opens away Dec 5.

items.name: Washington Huskies men's basketball
items.note: one aggregator lists home games *Dec 8 (Southern Utah)*, the day after the trip, then Dec 13 UCLA and Dec 19 Baylor.

items.name: Seattle Mariners (MLB)
items.note: season runs April to September. In December, ballpark tours are the only option.

items.name: Seattle Sounders FC (MLS)
items.note: season runs late February to October/November.

items.name: Seattle Reign FC (NWSL)
items.note: season runs March to November.

items.name: Seattle Storm (WNBA)
items.note: season runs May to September.
